spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the Kephalaia Passage

---

**¶1**

At the time when the Divine Human as it first proceeded forth [GAP-1: into the natural and sensual degrees of creation] entrusted governance to the five essential faculties of the spiritual mind [GAP-2: through which it operates — and when] the Divine Rational Principle and the Celestial Matrix of all affectional life [GAP-3: together descended into the lower degrees] — for the whole dominion of divine order had become interwoven with natural and sensual states, and the good within it was bound fast as upon a cross [GAP-4: within the realm of opposition] — all things were diffused and commingled with one another: wisdom with falsity and falsity with wisdom.

---

**¶2**

At that time the Divine Rational Principle summoned one of its subordinate faculties, one abundantly endowed with spiritual power, and granted it governance over the external truths that clothe the interior life. Now this faculty itself [GAP-5: received its commission] of [GAP-6: the ordering of all outward forms, and] suspended them in their proper arrangement and established them [GAP-7: according to the design] of the Divine Providence [GAP-8: from which all order descends, and] set all things into their rightful stations [GAP-9: within the spiritual cosmos, and] opened [GAP-10: the successive degrees of] the ten discrete planes of spiritual order [GAP-11: through which influx descends, and arranged] the revolving system of knowledges of good and truth [GAP-12: so that each knowledge might illuminate according to its station among] them, and the [GAP-13: whole fabric of the ordered mind was established].

---

**¶3**

The Divine Rational Principle operates in this manner: Just as [GAP-14: a master builder] and an ordering intelligence might construct a dwelling-place for the Lord Himself, and divide it into distinct faculties and chambers of the mind, and [GAP-15: distinct degrees of reception,] providing everything that is needful for the form of heavenly good [GAP-16: within each faculty,] and purifies them — and also the foundational natural truths [GAP-17: are shaped and fitted among] them for the form of good and its beauty — and arranges and perfects them so that when the Lord comes and inhabits that mind as His dwelling, it might glorify Him through its reception of His life.

---

**¶4**

Furthermore, the Divine Providence resembles a wise and skilled former of the natural mind [GAP-18: who perceives the unformed natural good] before it was wrought upon [GAP-19: by any ordering truth,] before it was established and made beautiful and [GAP-20: brought into the form of use. This wise] former of the natural [GAP-21: already perceives what each capacity may become, and] works within it; yet [GAP-22: the finished form does not yet exist in the material, but exists] in Him, in His [GAP-23: foresight and] in His understanding. And He brings the power of discrimination and the instrument of analysis, and separates the undifferentiated natural good into distinct states [GAP-24: suited to their several uses,] and draws forth the [GAP-25: rough and uneven qualities, and smooths] it with the refining power and makes it even. He fashions many [GAP-26: distinct] forms receptive of divine influx, ordering them according to their kind; He distinguishes and produces vessels of reception from it — vessels of differing kinds, such as containing forms for nourishment and containing forms for sustenance. This natural good, which [GAP-27: was formerly shapeless and without use,] since previously it had not been wrought upon before it was sealed by the skill and wisdom of this dextrous Divine Providence — He distinguished it into different forms of use, each one serviceable to its Lord.

---

**¶5**

So it is also with the Divine Providence. In His wisdom He has [GAP-28: formed and ordered all things] in their organic members [GAP-29: and arranged every faculty of the] mind as His dwelling [GAP-30: placing each good and each truth] within it, whether in a [GAP-31: greater or lesser capacity of] use [GAP-32: — and He has fashioned] the vessels that convey wisdom across the expanse [GAP-33: and] all the other works of spiritual formation [GAP-34: He has completed and set in order] within the [GAP-35: whole of creation] — so that when the great Lord comes, He who is the Third Proceeding of the Divine — the Redemptive Presence — who [GAP-36: enters into all that has been prepared for Him,] He might dwell within this ordered creation as within His own [GAP-37: kingdom, and fill it with His life.]

---

**¶6**

[GAP-38: And all things so ordered shall] live. The wisdom, however, that is within the creation [GAP-39: He who is] wise gathers up and elevates to its proper heavenly state; but the refuse and the falsity from evil shall be collected together and cast down into the hell from which it arose.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: At the time when the F[ir]st [Man went down] he gave the leadership to his five [sons. Then the] Living Spirit and the Mother of Life [came down] as the entire ruling-power is entwined and crucified [in the Darkness, and] they were poured out and mixed with each other, the light with the Darkness and the Darkness with the light.

At that time the Living Spirit called one of his sons, one rich with power. He gave to him the leadership of the garments. Now, he himself [received the command] of [the garments, and] he hung them and set them up [by the command] of the Father of Life [who sent him. And] he set up all things [in the heights, and] he opened [out the] ten firmaments [and he set] the wheel of the stars [above] them and the [luminaries].

The Living Spirit is like this: Just as [a builder] and an architect who might build a dwelling for the king, and divide it up into separate houses and [separate rooms, and provides] everything that is required for beauty [in every room] and he cleans them. And also the stones [he shapes] them for beauty and loveliness, and he arranges them and makes them so that should the king come and inhabit that palace, he might glorify him.

Furthermore, the Father of Life resembles a wise and skilled carpenter [who finds a piece of wood] before it was worked [or shaped, and] before it was established and made beautiful and [useful. This] carpenter [knows what it shall become, and] works in it, but [it is] in him in his [thought and] in his understanding, and he brings the saw and the adze, and cuts it into separate pieces [and he trims] it and he pulls the [roughness from] it with the plane and he smooths it. He shall make many [kinds of] wooden implements, arranging them shape by shape; he cuts and produces wooden implements from it, wooden implements of different kinds, (such as) dishes, bowls. This wood, that [had no form] since previously it had not been worked before it was sealed by [the ski]ll and wisdom of this dextrous carpenter. He cut it up into different sorts of implements useful to his master.

So is it also with the Father of Life. In his wisdom he has [formed all things] in limbs [and built the] palace [and placed all things] in it or in a [vessel] useful [to him. He made] the ships of light [and] all the other works [that he established] in the [universe] so that when the great king comes, he who is the Third Ambassador, who [shall come to it] he might dwell in this universe [and purify it]
[And all things shall] live. The light, however, that is in it [he who is] wise, and he takes it up to the land; but the waste and the Darkness will be gathered and thrown down to the abyss.

fills.explanation: The First Man "went down" to battle the Darkness is the standard Manichaean cosmogonic formula, corresponding to the Divine Human proceeding forth into the natural and sensual degrees.

A temporal transition is needed between the First Man giving leadership to his five sons and the subsequent descent of the Living Spirit and Mother of Life, matching the Manichaean cosmogonic sequence.
The Living Spirit and Mother of Life descended into the lower degrees to rescue and order the creation, corresponding to the Divine Rational Principle descending to organize the natural mind.
The ruling-power was crucified "in the Darkness" (the realm of opposition), and then the mixture of light and darkness followed; the connector "and" bridges to the next clause.
The son rich with power received his commission from the Living Spirit, corresponding to a subordinate faculty receiving governance over the external truths.
The command concerns "the garments" (external truths/outward forms) previously mentioned, and the conjunction bridges to his actions of hanging and setting them up.
The cosmic structures were set up "by the command" of the Father of Life, corresponding to establishment according to the design of Divine Providence.
The Father of Life is identified as the one who sent the son, corresponding to the source from which all order descends, with "And" connecting to the next action.
All things were set up "in the heights" (within the spiritual cosmos), with "and" connecting to the next act of opening the firmaments.
He "opened out the" ten firmaments — a standard cosmogonic expression for establishing the successive discrete planes of spiritual order.
After opening the firmaments, the next cosmogonic act is setting/arranging the wheel of the stars, corresponding to arranging the revolving system of knowledges.
The wheel of the stars was set "above" the firmaments, corresponding to the knowledges of good and truth illuminating from their station over the ordered planes.
The final element completing the cosmic arrangement after firmaments and stars is the luminaries (sun and moon), corresponding to the whole fabric of the ordered mind being established.
Paired with "an architect," "a builder" provides the manual counterpart to the designer, together forming the "master builder" of the spiritual reading.
The palace is divided into houses and rooms (distinct degrees of reception), and the builder provides everything needed for beauty within each space.
The beauty is furnished "in every room" of the palace, corresponding to the provision of heavenly good within each faculty of the mind.
The builder shapes the foundational stones for beauty, corresponding to the foundational natural truths being shaped and fitted for the form of good.

fills.fill: who finds a piece of wood
fills.explanation: The carpenter parable begins with finding raw, unworked wood, corresponding to the Divine Providence perceiving unformed natural good before it has been wrought upon.
The wood had not been worked "or shaped" before being established — parallel terms for the unformed state prior to any ordering truth being applied.
Before the wood was made beautiful and useful (brought into the form of use), the carpenter already perceived its potential; "This" restarts the sentence introducing the carpenter's foresight.

fills.fill: knows what it shall become, and
fills.explanation: The carpenter already perceives what each capacity of the wood may become, corresponding to Divine foresight knowing the potential of each faculty before working upon it.
The finished form does not yet exist in the wood, but "it is" in the carpenter — the design exists in his mind before it exists in the material.
The form exists in the carpenter's "thought and" understanding — two parallel mental faculties corresponding to foresight and comprehension.
After cutting into separate pieces, the carpenter trims each piece to suit its intended use, corresponding to forming states suited to their several purposes.
The carpenter pulls the "roughness from" the wood with the plane, corresponding to removing the rough and uneven qualities from the natural good through refinement.
He makes many "kinds of" wooden implements, corresponding to the distinct forms receptive of divine influx, ordered by type.
The wood "had no form" before being worked — it was formerly shapeless and without use, corresponding to unformed natural good prior to divine ordering.
In his wisdom the Father of Life has "formed all things" in limbs, corresponding to the Divine Providence having formed and ordered all organic members of creation.
After forming all things in limbs, the Father of Life "built the" palace, corresponding to arranging every faculty of the mind as the divine dwelling.
The Father "placed all things" in the palace, corresponding to placing each good and each truth within the ordered mind.
Each thing is placed in the palace or in a "vessel" useful for its purpose, corresponding to a capacity of reception — directly echoing the carpenter's wooden implements as vessels.
The vessels are useful "to him" (the master/Lord), and then a new clause begins: "He made the ships of light," corresponding to fashioning the vessels that convey wisdom.
A simple conjunction connecting "the ships of light" to "all the other works" in a list of what the Father of Life fashioned.
All the other works "that he established" in the universe — a relative clause identifying the works as completed and set in order by the Father of Life.
The works are established "in the universe" — the standard Kephalaia term for the whole of creation, the cosmic dwelling-place prepared for the divine king.
The Third Ambassador "shall come to it" — entering into what has been prepared for him, corresponding to the Redemptive Presence entering the ordered creation.

The Third Ambassador dwells in the universe "and purifies it" — the standard Manichaean description of the Ambassador's function of extracting light, corresponding to filling creation with divine life.
The concluding statement "And all things shall live" describes how all things so ordered by Divine Providence receive life through the divine indwelling.
The light in creation is gathered by "he who is" wise — a divine epithet identifying the one who elevates wisdom to its proper heavenly state.
